newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 13.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Wednesday:
- The economy will continue to grow rapidly for the next 18 months as long as the government does not "mess it up," according to Terry Baker, economist at the Economic and Social Research Institute.
- A review of Radio Ireland, the struggling national broadcaster which has announced plans to revamp its schedule, is to be carried out by the Independent Radio and Television Commission.
- The murder of a barman in Limerick city centre early yesterday may have been linked to his opposition to drug dealers trying to use the pub where he worked.
- Sinn Fein's Martin McGuinness was described as the "godfather of godfathers" by the Ulster Unionist Party's security spokesman Ken Maginnis during a live television debate last night.
- Bigger tax cuts could be the key to prolonging Ireland's economic miracle, the Economic and Social Research Institute suggested yesterday.
- Supporters of singer Dana's bid for the presidency have targeted 60 Fianna Fail and Fine Gael politicians they believe may be prepared to nominate her.
- The government is to consider the introduction of a register of sex offenders which would include details of the type of offence committed and the offender's name and address.
- Troubled Radio Ireland was in crisis last night after new listenership figures show it has achieved just a one percent share of the national audience.
- Limerick police were last night trying to establish the motive for the brutal murder of a 58-year barman whose body was found in a laneway in the city centre yesterday.

- Health concerns over the presence of toxic blue-green algae in Killarney's largest lake have led the Munster Regional Trout Angling Council to cancel a number of events scheduled for the lake in late August and early September.
- A major rescue plan is being drawn up by Radio Ireland after the latest listenership survey shows the new independent national radio station with just one percent of market share.
